svg.title: How to build systems that can contain a breach
svg.desc: Nine practices for when attackers log in with stolen credentials. 1. Design the security experience: Tell customers what happened, why, and how to recover; 2. Build security circuit breakers: Suspicious bulk actions pause automatically, not just alert; 3. Design for partial unavailability: Suspend one tenant or operation, not the whole service; 4. Make operations interruptible: Long-running work can pause, cancel or reauthorize; 5. Add friction when behavior looks suspicious: Scoped keys, rate limits, less concurrency, extra auth; 6. Make restrictions survive failover: Retries, queues and backups can't route around them; 7. Measure false positives: Track interruptions, how long they last, how fast customers recover; 8. Test containment, not just detection: Simulate stolen credentials and confirm the damage stops; 9. Design for recovery: Restrictions are reversible; interrupted work resumes safely. By Doug Tarr, douglastarr.com.
